 Order

Petitioner being the beneficiary of acquisition of subsoil rights in the land belonging to the respondents, is knocking at the doors of Writ Court for assailing the judgment & award entered by the learned Prl. District & Sessions Judge, Chitradurga whereby, land owners Misc.No.374/2012 having been filed under section 10(2) of The Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962 (hereafter '1962 Act'), having been favoured, the compensation has been enhanced to Rs.12,61,968/- with usual statutory benefits.

entities.text: Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
2. Learned Sr. Panel Counsel appearing for the petitioner-Company seeks to falter the impugned judgment & award arguing that:
(i) The petition u/s 10(2) of the 1962 Act filed by the respondents claiming enhancement of compensation was apparently time barred, limitation period being 90 days and therefore, no relief could have been granted to them.
(ii) In the meeting of land owners, it was unanimously resolved to pay certain sums of money at the rate of five times the guideline value along with admissible additions in respect of notified lands; all the land owners having concurred with the same, the respondents could not have petitioned the court below for enhancement of the compensation, because of estoppel.
(iii) The award of compensation by way of enhancement under several heads is much on the higher side and this is because of the invocation of the provisions of the erstwhile Land Acquisition Act, 1894; this could not have been done when the 1962 Act is a complete code in itself; and (iv) The extent of land notified for acquisition of subsoil rights and accordingly acquired is only 11 guntas whereas the court below has re-determined it to be 18 guntas absolutely without any basis and therefore, the award of compensation in respect of land in excess of what is notified, is unsustainable.
3. Learned counsel appearing for the respondents per contra contended that:
(i) The question of limitation would pale into insignificance when the subsoil rights of the land in question were notified for acquisition in the name of a dead person and without making any enquiry.

(ii) The compensation awarded perfectly accords with just compensation and Gail (India) Ltd vs Competent Authority Under The Pmp Act on 10 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81340573/

3 therefore, regardless of arguable lacuna in respect of certain heads under which enhancement is made, no grievance can be made against the impugned judgment &
award.
(iii) The invocability of the provisions of 1894 Act cannot be found fault with.

Compensation is payable for the rights taken in respect of the land and therefore, if the land taken is more than what is notified, the award of compensation for the excess land taken is perfectly in accordance with law & justice.
(iv) What was decided in the meeting of the other land owners does not bind respondents who were neither parties nor invitees to the meetings.

Even otherwise,
right to compensation for the subsoil of the land acquired has the trappings of constitutional guarantee under Article 300A.
(v) The issues raised by the petitioner-company are fact-specific and therefore, a Writ Court exercising a limited supervisory jurisdiction constitutionally vested under Article 227, cannot undertake a deeper examination of the same, unlike a court of appeal.
4.
This matter was taken up for final hearing with the consent of both the sides.

Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having perused the Petition Papers, this court declines indulgence in the matter for the following reasons:
(a) As to bar of limitation:
(i) The first contention of the petitioner as to bar of limitation for filing the petition under section 10(2) of the 1962 Act cannot be countenanced since the land was notified in the name of a dead person, and award too was passed in the name of said person; admittedly, no notices were served on the L.Rs of the deceased; apparently,
they had no opportunity of petitioning u/s 10(2) of the Act within the alleged period of limitation of 45 days.
If the acquisition proceedings were accomplished taking the name of a person who was living then, such a contention would have gained acceptance.
Violation of substantive rights is one thing and launching the legal battle for redressal is another; the former is a matter of substantive law whereas the latter is of adjective law.
All adjective laws have to be construed liberally subject to all just exceptions into which argued case of the petitioner does not fit.

Where acquisition proceedings were initiated & accomplished in the name of a dead person, the period of limitation for working out the grievance commences from the date of knowledge of the legal representatives, especially when the provision for condonation of delay is conspicuously absent.
An argument to the contrary is repugnant to the rules of reason & justice.
No rule or ruling is cited from the side of petitioner to discredit this general norm of adjudication.

Gail (India) Ltd vs Competent Authority Under The Pmp Act on 10 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81340573/
4
(ii) The right to property is constitutionally guaranteed u/a 300A as expansively interpreted by the Apex Court in K.T.PLANTATION PRIVATE LIMITED vs. STATE OF KARNATAKA (2011) 9 SCC 1.

entities.text: K.T.PLANTATION PRIVATE LIMITED vs. STATE OF KARNATAKA (2011) 9 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The State can acquire private property for public purpose, is true;
however, it is conditioned by the payment of compensation.
Right to compensation which includes right to enhancement of compensation, is also guaranteed u/a 300A.
The prescription of limitation period for launching a legal battle for enhancement of compensation has to be construed in the light of constitutional guarantee.

The State u/a 12 of the Constitution and its instrumentalities like the petitioner-Company vide AJAY HASIA vs. KHALID MUJIB SEHRAVARDI, (1981) 1 SCC 722,
cannot defeat the constitutional rights of the citizens on unsure grounds of adjective/procedural law.

entities.text: AJAY HASIA vs. KHALID MUJIB SEHRAVARDI, (1981) 1 SCC 722
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A contra argument offends the spirit of constitutional guarantees.

The Apex Court in STATE OF PUNJAB vs. SHAMLAL MURARI, 1976 SCR (2) 82, has observed:
"...Processual law is not to be a tyrant but a servant, not an obstruction but an aid to justice.

entities.text: STATE OF PUNJAB vs. SHAMLAL MURARI, 1976 SCR (2) 82
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Procedural prescriptions are the hand-maid and not the mistress, a lubricant,
not a resistant in the administration or justice."
(iii) As already mentioned above, the acquisition of land can be done only in accordance with law namely the various provisions under the 1962 Act.

The land could not have been notified for acquisition in the name of a dead person; minimum enquiry as to whether khaataadaar is alive or not, should be undertaken where land is being acquired under the special statute; mindless exercise affects the constitutional guarantees availing to citizens.
At least in the land owners meeting, the petitioner ought to have ascertained the absence of anyone from the side of owner of the subject land.
That has not been done in the matter nor any explanation is offered for not doing it.
Allowing contention of the kind would amount to placing premium on illegality namely notifying the land in the name of a deceased owner.
Therefore, the contention as to bar of limitation is liable to be rejected, regardless of arguable lacuna in the impugned judgment, in this connection.
This court hastens to add that it is not sure if section 29(2) of the Limitation Act, 1963 was readily invocable.

(b) As to meeting of land owners and estoppel:
The vehement submission of the Sr. Panel Counsel for the petitioner that in the land owners meeting convened by the Deputy Commissioner of Chitradurga on 12.7.2011 & 10.8.2011, there was a consensus arrived at as to payment of compensation at five times the existing land rates, malkies by 30% of the guideline values and therefore, the respondents are estopped from petitioning for enhancement of compensation, is bit difficult to agree with and reasons for this are not far to seek:
there is no material placed on record that any notice of meeting was sent to the respondents herein nor that they had participated in the meeting.
There is no scope for assuming knowledge of the said meetings when the acquisition proceedings were accomplished in the name of a dead person.
Even otherwise, no material is placed to vouch the contention that the respondents herein having participated in the meeting, have consented to what has been resolved therein.

When right to petition for enhancement of compensation is guaranteed under the Gail (India) Ltd vs Competent Authority Under The Pmp Act on 10 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81340573/
5 - 10 - 1962 Act, the plea of estoppel cannot be readily invoked without demonstrating the foundational facts therefor.

Even if a little evidentiary material was placed on record to prima facie show the participation of respondents or their nominee in the meeting of the land owners, that could have weighed with this court.

(c) As to enhancement of compensation being on the higher side:
(i) A host of factors enter the fray while determining the compensation or re-determining the same on a petition being presented for enhancement.

Some guess work as of necessity enters the fray and there cannot be mathematical accuracy in working out the compensation, more particularly when what is acquired is not the land as such but its subsoil for the purpose of laying the pipelines.
At times, the using of subsoil nearly amounts to depriving the land itself almost in an entirety when it is rendered useless for cultivation because of various factors.
What court has to see is broadly what is awarded by section 10(2) court is just & reasonable in the conspectus of the case.
- 11 - (ii) Section 10 employs a wide phraseology.
It provides for the payment of compensation for any damage, loss or injury sustained by any person interested in the land and thus, obviously the owner is included.
As already mentioned above, it is not a case of acquisition of land but the acquisition in a sense of the subsoil so that pipelines can be laid, keeping the surface of the land intact.

Gail (India) Ltd vs Competent Authority Under The Pmp Act on 10 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81340573/
6 - 12 - It broadly prescribes the factors which section 10(2) court has to advert to while adjudging the petition for enhancement of compensation.
The succinct table of heads under which the compensation has been paid broadly accords with the parameters of section 10(3).
The breakup of enhancement of compensation under various heads has been furnished in a tabular form in the impugned judgment.
The same is reproduced hereunder for ease of reference:

Sl.No. Heads Amounts in Rs.
 1 Towards acquisition (user of) Rs.1,76,418/-
 land for 18 guntas in  2 Towards destruction of trees Rs.2,50,000/-
 3 Towards destruction of tombs Rs.4,04,096/-
4 Destruction
of pond

5 Destruction of embankment Rs.73,199/-
 6 Destruction of fence Rs.63,130/-
7 Destruction
of borewell and Rs.20,000/-
hand-pump

8 Destruction of cattle-shed Rs.50,000/-
 9 Destruction of crops Rs.15,000/-
 10 Towards diminution of land Rs.1,00,000/-
 Total Rs.12,61,968/-

These heads have been discussed by the learned Judge in the course of the judgment and they are not shown to fall foul of the law despite vociferous arguments submitted on - 13 - behalf of the petitioner-Company.
This court being a court of supervisory jurisdiction with restriction limitations, cannot treat the matter as if it is sitting in appeal over the orders of the court below.
A microscopic examination may yield some points for arguments, on either side.

However,
that is not the purpose of adjudication in writ jurisdiction.

Even if there are some arguable errors,
that per se would not invalidate the impugned decision when examination is under Article 227 vide SADHANA LODH vs. NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED, (2003) 3 SCC 524, Article 226 being ornamentally employed in the petition.

entities.text: SADHANA LODH vs. NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED, (2003) 3 SCC 524
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
(d) As to extent of the land regardless of notification:
(i) The land to the extent of 11 guntas was notified and accordingly, award too came to be passed by the competent authority, is true.
It was the grievance of the respondents in their petition filed u/s 10(2) of the 1962 Act that the land used is far in excess of what is notified.

Gail (India) Ltd vs Competent Authority Under The Pmp Act on 10 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81340573/
7
That led to the court below making endeavor to ascertain what is the actual extent of land used.
This it did not on the guess work, but on the basis of cogent evidentiary - 14 - material placed on record, more particularly, exhibits P6 (gazette notification), P8 (award) & P14 (survey sketch).
There was other evidentiary material, in addition.
What is payable as compensation is for the land taken regardless of what is notified being lesser in extent.
Section 2 which provides for the payment of compensation employs the word 'land' in too many places and what is conspicuously absent is the expression 'land as notified' or the like.
A notification wrongly mentioning lesser extent of land cannot deprive the owner of the compensation for the larger extent of land that is actually taken.
A reverse proposition would cut short the constitutional guarantee u/a 300A.
( ii )
It is relevant to see the discussion at paragraphs 13 & 14 of the judgment:
"13. The advocate for the petitioners relied upon Ex.P.6 Gazette Notification.
As per the said document, respondents have acquired 1.0197 Hectares in Sy.No.50 of Gannayakanahally village.

As per Ex.P.14 survey sketch issued by the respondents,
the respondents have acquired land measuring 2 Acre 20 guntas and they have paid compensation to an extent of 2 acre 29 guntas which is more than the extent shown in Ex.P.6 Gazette Notification, but the respondents - 15 - have not explained anything as to difference of measurement shown in survey sketch and Gazette Notification in respect of Survey No.50.
Even as per Ex.P.8 award, the respondents have not explained anything in this regard.

As per Ex.P.14 survey sketch and other documents, the respondents have acquired initially land measuring 2 acre 20 guntas then it was strike out and shown the extent as 2 acre 29 guntas, for that the respondents have not explained...(sic)
14.

Therefore, considering all these facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the clear opinion that the respondents have erected pipeline in the land bearing Sy.No.20/1 measuring 18 guntas, caused damage to the graveyards, trees, borewell,
hand pump, bund etc.
The respondents have not drawn mahazar at spot in the presence of the witnesses or in the presence of the petitioners.
The respondents have not paid adequate compensation..."
(iii) Learned Judge of the court below in the course of the judgment has referred to certain principles relatable to the provisions of erstwhile 1894 Act, is true.
The contention of the petitioner that the 1962 Act being a complete code, the court below could not have invoked the provisions of 1894 Act, appears to be too farfetched an argument.
The text & context of section 18 of the 1962 Act comes handy for repelling such a contention.

The same reads as under:
Gail (India) Ltd vs Competent Authority Under The Pmp Act on 10 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81340573/
8 - 16 - "18. Application of other laws not barred.--
The provisions of this Act shall be in addition to and not in derogation of any other law for the time being in force relating to acquisition of land."

The 1894 Act had been there for more than a century till it came to be repealed by The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 w.e.f. 1.1.2014.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Even otherwise, the 1894 Act is treated by the courts as the broad framework of law for acquisition of private property for public purpose on payment of compensation.
Law Reports are replete with instances where courts in determining the compensation for the land acquired under special statutes, have copiously made use of the provisions of 1894 Act.
(iv) Apparently, the petitioner is invoking the equitable jurisdiction of this court where conduct of the litigants assumes significance.

Notifying the land in the name of a dead person and taking the land far in excess of what is notified and trying to deny enhancement of compensation to the respondents without ascertaining whether they had attended farmers meeting and had agreed to the Resolution passed therein, do not augur well - 17 - with the State entities u/a 12.
An otherwise right judgment does not become unsustainable merely because some provisions of law have been wrongly invoked.
A constitutional court exercising equitable jurisdiction u/a 227 has to see not just whether the impugned order is wrong but whether on its overall examination, it is unsustainable.

If the wrong order has brought about a right result,
the navigational modalities largely loose significance, certain arguable infirmities therein,
notwithstanding.
By no stretch of imagination, it can be contradicted that what has been awarded is just & reasonable compensation, in the days when land prices have skyrocketed post 1990 era.

Regard being had to all the factors, the award of interest at the rate of 12% on additional market value of the property for the period between 13.4.2010 & 10.10.2011 and 9% from 11.9.2011 i.e.,
taking of possession and 15% per annum for the subsequent period, cannot be faltered, in view of section 28 of the 1894 Act.

- 18 - In the above circumstances, this Writ Petition being devoid of merits, is liable to be dismissed &
accordingly, it is, costs having been made easy.
Sd/-
JUDGE BSV/
